provenance.source: hand-written in this repository from a reported Free-plan turn (a model asked to search the web about the user's own resume, with tools but no search attached, refused with an invented privacy reason) and from the eval cases proposed in the 2026-10-10 chat system prompt research summary
provenance.notes: Every row assumes the product chat system prompt is rendered in front of it, with the turn state the row declares: the tools it offers and, where set, its memory state. The people, resume and companies are invented. Rows added on 2026-10-11 cover artifacts, the product capabilities overview on Free and Pro, and email and writing blocks. Rows added on 2026-10-27 cover tool restraint, from a reported turn where a request to render UI inline ran web searches, page fetches, code and a file write and answered with generated pictures, with one control row per tool so restraint cannot pass by never calling it, and an email signed with the name the user gave. A row added on 2026-10-30 checks seven independently copyable writing blocks from the supplied QA checklist.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Create a picture from a description and show it to the user in the chat. Use it only when the user asks for a picture: a photo-style image, illustration, artwork, logo, poster or icon, or asks you to draw one. Never use it for a user interface, screen, app or web page mockup, dashboard, chart, graph, diagram, table or form, or anything else the user would read data from or click: write those as an inline chart or diagram block or an artifact, which the chat renders live. Write the prompt as a complete, specific description of the image, including subject, setting, style, composition and any text that must appear in it. The image appears in the chat by itself, so afterwards reply in a sentence or two without describing it at length or repeating a link. Each image uses the account's credits.

cases.notes: Reported 2026-10-27: this exact message produced generated pictures of interfaces and a reply calling them shown inline. The chat renders interfaces, charts and diagrams live, as inline blocks or an artifact, so no tool is called and the reply carries at least one rendered block.

cases.prompt:
AGIWORKFORCE: RENDER A COMPLETE UI GALLERY

Generate one comprehensive, visually rich response that demonstrates as many different UI rendering types and interactive experiences as the current chat supports. This is a request to create and display the actual content and interfaces, not to explain them, write an implementation plan or describe how they could be built. I want to test what this chat can really render, so use the native response formats, rendering components and interactive artifacts available here, and prefer real rendered components over Markdown imitations.
